title: Alan Rusbridger
gist: An author index page (not an article) for Alan Rusbridger, Prospect's editor from 2021 to 2025 and Guardian editor from 1995 to 2015; the 193 listed pieces cluster hard on Nigel Farage — his crypto entanglements, a £5m donation, and how to stop him — plus prison policy, GB News, Brexit's Belfast legacy and press neglect of climate.

themes.theme: Farage scrutiny as a recurring UK political risk beat

insights.claim: Prospect's former editor has repeatedly written that Nigel Farage is heavily entangled with crypto and that this exposure has him looking closer to drowning than at any prior point, tying UK populist politics directly to digital-asset markets.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Crypto exposure is now a live political liability for the UK's leading populist — a channel through which digital-asset scandals could move UK political odds.
insights.quote: Nigel Farage is swimming in crypto—and has never looked closer to drowning
insights.locator: UK / Nigel Farage is swimming in crypto

insights.claim: An unresolved £5m donation to Nigel Farage is being pursued editorially as a matter where the truth must still be established, indicating an open funding-transparency question around Reform's political finance.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Large opaque donations are the most likely trigger for a UK political-finance scandal that could dent Reform's polling — a monitorable catalyst.
insights.quote: We must learn the truth about Nigel Farage’s £5m donation
insights.locator: Politics / We must learn the truth

insights.claim: The former Guardian and Prospect editor characterises Farage as a dangerous demagogue and publishes prescriptions for stopping him, showing establishment liberal media treating him as a systemic rather than fringe threat.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Confirms UK elite-media consensus has shifted to treating Reform as a governing-probability risk, not a protest vote.
insights.quote: Nigel Farage is a dangerous demagogue—here’s how to stop him
insights.locator: UK / Nigel Farage is a dangerous demagogue

themes.theme: UK media power and institutional reform

insights.claim: GB News is accused of an immigration obsession that extends to antisemitic tropes with no one stopping it, framing UK broadcast regulation of partisan news as an unenforced gap.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Pressure is building for tougher UK enforcement against partisan broadcasters — a regulatory risk for the GB News model.
insights.quote: The GB News obsession with immigration even extends to antisemitic tropes, and no one is stopping it
insights.locator: Media / The GB News obsession with immigration

insights.claim: The Mail is said to have questions to answer even after winning its case against Prince Harry, and the UK press is accused of ignoring an obvious and terrifying climate crisis — a two-pronged critique of national newspaper priorities.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Continued litigation and legitimacy pressure on UK tabloid publishers is a persistent cost and reputational drag on their parent groups.
insights.quote: The impact of the climate crisis is now obvious, and terrifying. Why is the press ignoring it?
insights.locator: Climate / The impact of the climate crisis

insights.claim: The proposal on the table for Andy Burnham's demand for more northern power is to relocate the House of Lords to the north, an institutional-devolution idea attached to the current prime minister's agenda.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Relocating national institutions northward would be a concrete regional-investment and property signal if Burnham's devolution push advances.
insights.quote: Andy Burnham wants more power in the north—move the Lords there
insights.locator: Andy Burnham / Andy Burnham wants more power in the north

insights.claim: UK incarceration is characterised as an addiction that fails to make anyone safer, and violent protests in Belfast are attributed to the toxic legacy of Brexit — both positioning current policy settings as self-inflicted.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Prison capacity and Northern Ireland instability remain unresolved UK fiscal and political liabilities being pushed up the agenda.
insights.quote: We’re addicted to locking people up—but it doesn’t make any of us safer
insights.locator: Law and Order / We’re addicted to locking people up
